uncited: Unlike generic image compression [PngCompression](11785-pngcompression.md) which treats data as uniform pixel grids, these methods exploit the structured, heterogeneous nature of splat attributes (position, scale, rotation, amplitude) using spatial bucketing, delta encoding, and targeted quantization policies to achieve significant size reductions while maintaining rendering fidelity.
**Redundancy Exploitation:** The core principle is to identify and eliminate redundancy in the volumetric data.
**Transformation/Encoding:** Data is transformed into a domain where redundancy is more apparent or compact.
**Quantization (Lossy):** For lossy compression, continuous or high-precision values are mapped to a discrete set of representatives.
This approach leverages the spatial coherence of the projected attributes to achieve high compression ratios.
The need for efficient compression in 3D Gaussian Splatting arises from the large memory footprint of raw Gaussian primitives.

detail: The Self-Organizing Gaussians (SOG) approach further simplified the pipeline by projecting attributes to 2D for standard image codec compatibility [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the Self-Organizing Gaussians (SOG) approach projects attributes to 2D for standard image codec compatibility. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Self-Organizing Gaussians (SOG): project all attributes into 2D maps so we can use PNG/JPEG/EXR-style image codecs.' This matches the claim exactly.
